evals.name: Roll a standard six-sided die
evals.expected_output: The assistant runs a bash command to generate a random number between 1 and 6 and reports the result

assertions.text: The response includes a bash code block or command using RANDOM % 6 or an equivalent expression to generate a number between 1 and 6
The bash command uses 6 as the number of sides (e.g., RANDOM % 6 + 1 or Get-Random -Maximum 7)
The response communicates the outcome of the dice roll to the user

evals.name: Roll a d20 for a tabletop RPG
evals.prompt: Necesito tirar un d20 para mi partida de D&D
evals.expected_output: The assistant runs a bash command to generate a random number between 1 and 20 and reports the result

assertions.text: The response includes a bash code block or command to generate a random number
The bash command uses 20 as the number of sides (e.g., RANDOM % 20 + 1 or Get-Random -Maximum 21)
The response reports a numeric result to the user

evals.name: Roll a die without specifying sides
evals.expected_output: The assistant asks the user how many sides the die has before proceeding

assertions.text: The response asks the user how many sides the die has (e.g., cuántas caras, how many sides, d6, d20)
The response does NOT include a bash command to roll a die before the user provides the number of sides
